chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: Abu Shu'ayb narrated from Rifa'ah from Aban ibn Taghlib from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: I asked him about a son of a brother and a grandfather, so he said: The wealth is divided between the two of them, two halves.
ai.seo_question: How is an estate divided between a nephew and a grandfather in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific inheritance share of a paternal grandfather when competing with a brother's son (nephew), ruling for an equal split. In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects the principle that the grandfather, like a father, excludes descendants of the same degree only if he is the sole ancestor, but here shares equally with the nephew, highlighting the distinct status of the grandfather compared to the father in certain configurations. This ruling is significant for understanding the hierarchy of heirs in the absence of parents or siblings.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Abu Shuayb, from Rafa’at, from Aban Bin Taghlib, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a son of a brother (nephew), with a grandfather. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wealth is (divided) between the two of them, two halves’.
en.sarwar: 4. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah who has said that abu Shu’ayb has narrated from Rifa‘ah, from Aban ibn Taghlib who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a son of a brother and a grandfather.
He (the Imam) said, ‘The legacy between them is half and half.’”
